title: The Fox and the Lion

full_text:
A young fox who had never seen a lion encountered the King of Beasts on a woodland trail. The lion's thunderous stride and massive mane terrified the fox so utterly that he collapsed in the bushes, nearly dying of fright.

A month later, the fox met the lion a second time. He still felt deep dread, but this time he remained on his feet, hiding behind an oak tree and watching the great beast pass without trembling.

When they met for the third time, all fear had vanished from the fox's heart. He walked boldly up to the lion, tipped his hat, and engaged the King of the Forest in a polite, cheerful conversation about the weather, proving that understanding and experience conquer the terror of the unknown.
moral: Familiarity takes away the terrors of the unknown; courage grows through understanding.
